explanations.explanation: Sinai is the spot, baker! Verse 1 says the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. Moses is Israel's leader, and he's about to get a very big counting job. Picture it: the whole camp is out in the desert, and the LORD says, 'Take a census.' I'd be nervous, friend. I can't even count the crumbs on my counter without losing my place.

I see why you'd grab that one, friend, because Israel does camp in the plains of Moab later on (Numbers 22:1). But we're at the start of the book, and verse 1 says the LORD spoke to Moses in the Wilderness of Sinai. Right pin, different spot on the map. Moab's chapter hasn't come up yet, so it's still in the oven.

Zin is a wilderness too, so that was a fair guess. Later the whole congregation of Israelites enters the Wilderness of Zin (Numbers 20:1). But in this passage, verse 1 says the LORD spoke to Moses in the Tent of Meeting in the Wilderness of Sinai. Zin will have to wait its turn.
Yes! God says to list "…every man by name, one by one." (Numbers 1:2) Not a tally mark, not a guess. A name. I think that's a pretty good sign every man in that crowd counted.

Rank sounds like army talk, I get it. But God says to list "…every man by name, one by one." (Numbers 1:2) Nobody gets counted by how high up they are. Every man goes down on the list by his own name, from the top of the crowd to the back.

Trade would be one way to sort a crowd, but that's not what God asks for. Verse 2 says to list "…every man by name, one by one." The records also go by clans and families (Numbers 1:18), but the instruction here is the name. If I were in that line, I'd want my name read out loud, mustache and all.

explanations.answer: Men twenty or older who can serve in the army
explanations.explanation: That's the one. Verse 3 says to number those twenty years of age or older, everyone who can serve in Israel's army. Both parts matter: the age and the army. Plenty of people in Israel aren't on this list.

explanations.answer: Men thirty or older who can serve at the tent
explanations.explanation: Close on the shape of it, but the numbers and the job are off. Verse 3 says twenty years of age or older, and it says everyone who can serve in Israel's army. So the tent isn't the job here. This list is about the army.

explanations.answer: Every firstborn son from every single family
explanations.explanation: That would make a short list and a lot of grumpy younger brothers. But God says to number those twenty years of age or older, everyone who can serve in Israel's army (Numbers 1:3). Firstborn or not doesn't decide it. Age and the army do.

Not quite, friend. God says, "You and Aaron are to number those…" (Numbers 1:3), so Moses has Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), right beside him. Then God adds that one man from each tribe, the head of each family, must be there too (Numbers 1:4). So Moses is nowhere near doing it alone.

That's right. God tells Moses, "You and Aaron are to number those…" (Numbers 1:3). Aaron is Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). And God adds that one man from each tribe, the head of each family, must be there with them (Numbers 1:4). It's a team job, and Moses gets a whole crew.

Yep. The LORD gives the order on the first day of the second month (Numbers 1:1). Then Moses and Aaron assemble the whole congregation on the first day of the second month (Numbers 1:18). Same date, friend. They didn't sit on this one, and they didn't hit snooze either.

Check the dates and they match. The LORD speaks on the first day of the second month (Numbers 1:1). Then verse 18 says Moses and Aaron assembled the whole congregation on the first day of the second month. So it's the very same day the order came.

You got it. God says the Levites are to be appointed over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it (Numbers 1:50). So the Levites get a different kind of job than the army. They carry it, care for it, and camp around it.

Army makes sense, since that's what the rest of the census is about. But the Levites aren't counted with the army. God says to appoint them over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it (Numbers 1:50). Their post is at the tabernacle.

A storehouse sounds like a solid guess. But God never mentions one here. He says to appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the Testimony, all its furnishings, and everything in it (Numbers 1:50). That's a whole different kind of watch duty.

That's right. Verse 51 says whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites set it up. So taking it down and putting it up are both Levite jobs. I think that's a lot of packing for one tribe.

Not this time, friend. Verse 51 says, "Whenever the tabernacle is to move, the Levites are to take it down, and whenever it is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up." So the Levites do the setting up. No other tribe gets that job.

explanations.answer: He must be put to death
explanations.explanation: Yes, and it's a heavy one. God says, "Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death." (Numbers 1:51) That's the serious rule He gives for the tabernacle. The text says it plainly, so we do too.

explanations.answer: He must wash and wait until evening
explanations.explanation: Washing and waiting until evening sounds like a milder rule, and I understand the guess. But this verse is far more serious. God says, "Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death." (Numbers 1:51) It's a heavy line, and we'll leave it at what the text says.

explanations.answer: He must bring a lamb to the priest
explanations.explanation: A lamb sounds like an easy fix, friend. But that's not what verse 51 says. It says, "Any outsider who goes near it must be put to death." It's a heavy line, and the text gives no other way out.

explanations.answer: By divisions under their own standards
explanations.explanation: That's it. God says the Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and under his own standard (Numbers 1:52). So each group has its own spot and its own flag. No wandering around looking for your tent.

explanations.answer: All together in one single camp
explanations.explanation: One big pile of tents would be quite the sight. But verse 52 says, "The Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and under his own standard." So there's an order to it. Each division camps under its own standard.

explanations.answer: Wherever each family chooses to settle
explanations.explanation: That sounds a lot like finding a parking spot at the mall, friend. But God doesn't leave it to choice. He says each man is to camp by divisions, in his own camp and under his own standard (Numbers 1:52). The plan comes from Him.

explanations.answer: So no wrath falls on Israel
explanations.explanation: That's what God says. The Levites camp around the tabernacle of the Testimony and watch over it "…so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel." (Numbers 1:53) So the Levites' watch is for the whole congregation. The reason comes straight from God's own words.

explanations.answer: So no enemy carries it off
explanations.explanation: I can see why that one comes to mind, since guarding usually means enemies. But God gives a different reason. The Levites camp around it "…so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel." (Numbers 1:53) The text doesn't mention an enemy carrying it off.

explanations.answer: So the other tribes can rest
explanations.explanation: Rest would be nice, but that's not the reason God gives. The Levites camp around the tabernacle and watch over it "…so that no wrath will fall on the congregation of Israel." (Numbers 1:53) Their watch is about protecting the whole congregation.

Yes, and that's how the chapter ends. Verse 54 says, "Thus the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." That's a whole census, a camp plan and a job for the Levites, all carried out as commanded. Not bad for a crowd of over six hundred thousand men.

Not here, friend. The chapter closes with, "Thus the Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses." (Numbers 1:54) So the census, the Levites and the camp plan were all done the way He said.
